intent: The clickable row of a sidebar menu, an icon and a label that collapses to the icon alone in the icon rail.
typical_uses: A navigation link row, rendered over the app's link element
The trigger row of a workspace switcher or user menu in the header or the footer

dont_use_when.situation: An action button outside a sidebar menu
A row of a nested sub-menu

invariants.text: A direct `svg` child is sized to the small icon size and a direct `span` that is the last child truncates with an ellipsis; a bare text node does not truncate.
Collapsed to the icon rail the row becomes a 32px square and every direct child after the first is not displayed, so the icon has to be the first child.
`tooltip` is mounted only while the sidebar is collapsed on desktop; expanded or on mobile no tooltip is rendered.
`isActive` sets a bare `data-active` attribute and the active fill; it sets no `aria-current`.
While the row is the trigger of an open popup (it carries `data-popup-open`), it keeps the hover fill.

anti_patterns.dont: Rely on `isActive` to tell assistive tech the current page
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-current="page"` beside `isActive` on the current link row

anti_patterns.dont: Put the label before the icon, or set an inline `display` on a direct child
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep the icon first; an inline `display` outranks the rule that hides the other children in the icon rail

rtl.by: sidebar.module.css sets `text-align: left` on .menuButton and reserves the trailing space with the physical `padding-right`, so neither mirrors under a right-to-left direction

tooltip.states: tooltip is a string or an object of TooltipContent props
tooltip.because: The type is `string | TooltipContentProps`, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property. A string is the tooltip's whole content; an object is spread over TooltipContent, so it also overrides the default `side="right"` and `align="center"`.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's useRender takes an element or a function of the row's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is how the row renders as the app's link element.

good.title: The current page's link row, with a tooltip for the icon rail
A tall switcher row that stays lit while its menu is open

bad.title: Label first, icon second
bad.why: In the icon rail only the first child stays, so the collapsed row shows a clipped label and no icon.

companions.typed_by: cva(...), returns (props: VariantProps<typeof sidebarMenuButtonVariants> & { className?: string }) => string
companions.description: The variant and size class-name builder SidebarMenuButton uses; it does not set the `data-active` attribute the active fill reads, and the icon-rail rules only apply inside a Sidebar.

tooltip.description: Partially typed: SidebarMenuButtonTooltip | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property and none for this one; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.partially_typed_props. tooltip is a string or an object of TooltipContent props. The type is `string | TooltipContentProps`, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property. A string is the tooltip's whole content; an object is spread over TooltipContent, so it also overrides the default `side="right"` and `align="center"`.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's useRender takes an element or a function of the row's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is how the row renders as the app's link element.
